view: Monday's +31.48% was mainly NVDA-specific: NVDA beat SOX by 17.4 points and AMD and AVGO by 25-28 points after Jensen Huang was reinstated, and NVDA/SOX jumped 15.3% (14.93 to 17.21) in one session. That repairs most of the governance discount but not the longer de-rating (NVDA/SOX still -5.9% vs 13 weeks ago and -38.3% vs 52 weeks ago; YTD NVDA -13.06% vs SOX +31.55%). One session does not turn a relative trend. Tactical: Hold/Wait for the ratio to hold above 17.21 on weekly closes before treating this as a relative-strength turn.

evidence.point: Mon 2026-11-23: NVDA +31.48%, SOX +14.03%, SMH +15.03%, Nasdaq Comp +6.51%, SPX +4.73%, AMD +6.85%, AVGO +3.0%. NVDA beat SOX by 17.4 points, SMH by 16.5, AMD by 24.6 and AVGO by 28.5. This was an idiosyncratic move with a sector lift, the mirror image of the 2026-11-16 week when NVDA lagged.

On beta 1.94, SPX +4.73% implies about +9.2% for NVDA; the actual +31.48% leaves about 22 points of NVDA-specific gain. Part of SOX's +14.03% is itself NVDA (NVDA is a large SOX/SMH constituent; exact weight not in slice), so the ex-NVDA sector move was smaller than 14%. Judgment, not data.

NVDA/SOX 17.2141 at Monday's close vs 14.9288 at the last completed week: +15.3% in one session. Versus 18.289 13 weeks ago it is now only -5.9% (derived), and versus 27.9219 52 weeks ago -38.3% (derived). The official 13w/52w changes (-18.4% / -46.5%) use completed weekly closes and do not yet include Monday.

Longer horizons still show NVDA lagging, even after Monday: 1M NVDA -21.77% vs SOX -10.19%; 3M -21.79% vs -17.22%; YTD -13.06% vs SOX +31.55% and AMD +107.15%. The governance repair is in the price; the year-long rotation out of NVDA into the rest of AI semis is not reversed.

The 4.8-point figure is TradingView rolling 5-session Perf.W (NVDA +3.8 vs SOX -1.0), which still includes the 2026-11-17 to 11-20 losses. Week-to-date (from the 125.53 / 8408.59 Friday closes) NVDA is +31.5% vs SOX +14.0%, about 17.4 points. Use the week-to-date figure for the forming week.

Rotation inside AI semis: on Monday money went back into NVDA rather than into peers (AMD +6.85%, AVGO +3.0%, far below SOX). TSM and peer 1W/13W/52W figures are not in slice, so I cannot say whether the YTD rotation into AMD is reversing beyond one day. Unknown, not neutral.

Market backdrop relief: VIX 26.61 (-25.8%), S5TH 53.08% (+7.16), RSP/SPY 0.2946 with RSP 1M -1.97% vs SPY -4.95% (breadth better than the cap-weighted index over a month). Broader risk appetite helped, but it explains only a small part of NVDA's move.

I moved to 46/24/30: down higher because the year-long relative de-rating vs SOX is intact and late-Feb 2027 results are a binary event inside the window; up kept near base because the remaining relative gap vs 13 weeks ago (-5.9%) and vs peers YTD leaves catch-up room if governance stays settled.

After a key-person shock is reversed, relative strength usually snaps back quickly toward the pre-shock level and then trades on the pre-shock trend. Here the pre-shock trend was already down (the ratio fell for many weeks before the CEO exit), so I expect the snap-back to stall rather than extend. Before vs after earnings: before 2026-11-17 relative was negative but resettable by the print; after it the beat failed to re-anchor, and the reset came from governance, not fundamentals. That makes the repair more fragile than an earnings-led one.

notes_for_chair: Retrospective (readings_2026-11-22, close 2026-11-20). Signs that pointed to a sharp rebound: (1) the idiosyncratic gap was already shrinking - NVDA lagged SOX by 5.8 points in the week of 2026-11-16 vs 21.6 the week before, and on Fri 2026-11-20 NVDA fell only about 3.3 points more than SOX with AMD -13.25%, so the selling had become sector-wide de-risking; (2) the relative de-rating was extreme and fast (NVDA/SOX -46.5% over 52 weeks, NVDA/SPX -35.1% over 13 weeks), which leaves room for a violent snap-back if the stock-specific cause reverses; (3) beta and correlation to SOX were rising (0.62 / 0.64), so a sector bounce would carry NVDA; (4) capitulation-style backdrop: VIX 35.9 (+26%), SOX -17.13% and SPX -8.61% in a week; (5) the small conditional base rates (2W drop <= -15%: 0% down at 2W, 100% up at 13W). Signs that did not: NVDA/SOX was still making new lows (14.93) with no turn, my own rule (two weekly closes without a new ratio low) gave no signal, peer rotation data was missing, and Friday closed only 0.8% above its low. Bottom line: relative strength showed that the setup was stretched and could snap back sharply. It did not predict the catalyst, which was the board reversing the CEO exit. The size of the governance-driven relative discount turned out to measure how much could be recovered. My 2026-11-22 call (2W 35/25/40, Wait) was too bearish on direction.

Proposed lessons-log line (owner/chair to decide): 'When a single-name relative discount is driven by a reversible governance event, the size of the idiosyncratic gap is also the size of the snap-back; do not extrapolate a relative downtrend that comes from an event which can be undone.'

Ladder (proposal only; owner approval required; no orders): relative strength does not justify chasing at 165.05. If the chair keeps rungs, rungs inside the open gap 125.53-156.93 make sense only with a relative condition (NVDA/SOX not back below 14.93). Actual rung prices are not in my slice.

Overlap: ATR tail-widening and the oversold conditional base rates are the momentum/technical group; count once.

Pre-mortem: if this is badly wrong by March, the most likely reason is that the reinstatement ends the governance discount completely and the market rotates back from AMD/AVGO into NVDA to close the YTD gap (NVDA -13% vs SOX +32%), so the move goes far above 181.56. My down weight would then have been anchoring on the year-long relative downtrend.
